title: Nights with thunderstorms per year (days per year)

source.name: The Maracaibo Beacon (NASA Earthdata) and Florida thunderstorm climatology (NOAA National Weather Service, Tampa Bay)
source.publisher: NASA Earthdata and NOAA National Weather Service

notes: Nocturnal thunderstorms occur over Lake Maracaibo on average about 297 days a year, firing up to 28 flashes a minute for up to nine or ten hours after dusk. NOAA's National Weather Service puts interior central Florida - the stormiest part of the United States - at close to 100 thunderstorm days a year (80 to 90 on the coasts). Lake water there holds near 28-31 degrees Celsius year-round while cool air drains off the Perija and Merida ranges of the Andes onto it at night, which is what fires the storms after dark.
